objections.claim: The spec mandates the subset assertion "at module load, and again in `--selftest`", calling a violation "a build-time fault (the selftest fails), not a runtime degradation". But `bin/faff` eagerly requires every `lib/*.js` (the load-order constraint `cli-surface.js` documents), so an assertion that throws at module load turns a drifted `CLASSIFIER_TABLE` key into a crash of the entire `faff` CLI — every verb, not just `github-templates` — which contradicts the never-throw posture the spec otherwise holds as load-bearing ("a scanner that can throw would be a defect in the invariant").
objections.evidence: Spec, "The subset assertion (the mechanical half of the taxonomy share)" — "At module load, and again in `--selftest`, assert that…"; contrast the spec's own purity section ("Nothing it does can throw at the caller") and `native-map.js`'s reader posture in the supplied context.
objections.predicted_consequence: The first taxonomy rename (the exact event the assertion exists to catch) takes down every `faff` verb with an unhandled require-time throw, instead of failing one selftest — the failure mode lands on the widest possible blast radius at precisely the moment the table is being edited.

objections.claim: DONE requires "`classify` resolves `labels` before `name` before `about`", but no scenario constructs a template whose signals disagree across tiers (e.g. `name: Bug report` with `labels: [feature]` must classify `feature`), and no scenario classifies a file via its `about` field alone. A build that scans the signals in the wrong order (name first, or about before name) passes every listed scenario, including both holdouts — the holdout RFC case tests *table* order (spike before feature), not *signal* order.
objections.evidence: DONE item "classify resolves `labels` before `name` before `about`…" under "From HOW (behaviour)"; scenarios all use single-signal or agreeing-signal fixtures.
objections.predicted_consequence: done cannot be decided for the precedence criterion by the shipped scenario set; a reordered-signal build ships green.
